corrected_value.title_o: The universal and automatic association between brightness and positivity
corrected_value.authors_o: Specker; Leder; Rosenberg; Hegelmaier; Brinkmann; Mikuni; Kawabata

decisions.quote:
The present study is a pre-registered replication of a study by Specker et al. (2018) that tests the
hypothesis that brightness of colors is associated with positivity.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding identify Specker et al. (2018), 'The universal and automatic association between brightness and positivity' (Acta Psychologica, 186, 47-53, DOI: 10.1016/j.actpsy.2018.04.007) as the single original paper directly re-tested across Studies 1 and 2 (lines 14-15, 71-73, 471-476). Other cited works (e.g., Hemphill, 1996; Lakens et al., 2012, 2013; Schietecat et al., 2018) are discussed only as background context.

decisions.quote:
Our results showed an implicit association
between brightness and positivity in both Study 1 and Study 2, however, an explicit association between
brightness and positivity was only found in Study 2, thereby replicating 3 out of 4 effects.
decisions.location: Abstract, lines 15-17 (see also Study 1 Discussion, lines 161-167; Study 2 Discussion, lines 280-285)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding correctly classify the replication outcome as 'mixed'. Across the two studies re-testing Specker et al. (2018), the implicit association replicated in both Study 1 (dz = 1.73, p < .001) and Study 2 (dz = 4.07, p < .001) and the explicit association replicated in Study 2 (dz = 3.06, p < .001), whereas the explicit association in Study 1 was non-significant (t(14) = -0.90, p > .05). Although the explicit measure in Study 1 was newly added to Study 1's protocol (having been used in Study 2 of Specker et al., 2018), the authors explicitly evaluate it as a replication test of the original paper's brightness-positivity claim and explicitly state in Study 1 Discussion (lines 164-167) that 'Study 1 did not show an explicit effect for the association between brightness and positivity that should theoretically have been there, we therefore interpret this as a failure to replicate,' summarizing the overall replication across the paper (Abstract line 17; Study 2 Discussion lines 283-285; General Discussion lines 390-391) as replicating 3 out of 4 effects.

decisions.quote:
The present study is a pre-registered replication of a study by Specker et al. (2018) that tests the
hypothesis that brightness of colors is associated with positivity.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding classify the study as a 'replication'. The authors collected new experimental data from two independent samples of 15 participants at the University of Vienna (Study 1, lines 109-111; Study 2, lines 249-251) to directly re-test Study 1 and Study 2 of Specker et al. (2018).
